title: Keep kikx up to date
description: Check your kikx version, see whether a newer release exists, upgrade in place, and learn what an upgrade replaces and what it never touches.
outcomes: Check which kikx you have with the version option
See whether a newer release exists without installing it
Upgrade kikx in place with kikx upgrade
Know that an upgrade never touches kikx.toml or your files

checks.checked: You ran kikx upgrade with the check option

recap: The version option prints the kikx you have installed.
kikx upgrade with the check option only reports whether a newer release exists.
kikx upgrade downloads the release for your system from GitHub and replaces the kikx binary.
It never touches kikx.toml or any vendored file: those are yours.
A new version changes what future add, setup and apply commands render, never what you already have.

steps.intro: kikx ships new releases with new components and fixes. This practice machine has the release before the latest installed, so let's upgrade it.
steps.setup: First, a project, so we can see what an upgrade does to it. I set one up from the {template} template.
steps.files: Keep an eye on these files during the upgrade.
steps.version: Which kikx do you have? {flagVersion} tells you.
steps.versionLine: That's the installed version, read from GitHub releases for this practice machine.
steps.releases: Each release is published on GitHub with a binary for every system. kikx upgrade reads that list.
steps.check: Your turn. Ask whether a newer release exists, without installing it: kikx upgrade {flagCheck}.
steps.checkLine: It compares your version with the latest release and stops there.
steps.checkWhy: Handy in a script or before a busy day: nothing changes until you decide.
steps.upgrade: Your turn. Install it: type kikx upgrade and press Enter.
steps.upgraded: kikx downloaded the release for your system and replaced its own binary. Run the version option again any time to confirm.
steps.replaces: That's all it replaces: the kikx program itself, in the same place it was installed.
steps.untouched: Your project didn't change at all. Same files, same content.
steps.tomlSame: kikx.toml is exactly as before. An upgrade never edits a project.
steps.newTemplates: A new version can render components differently. That only affects the next add, setup or apply. To pick up a change, re-render one component with {flagForce}, or apply into a separate folder and compare.
steps.again: Run kikx upgrade again and it says you're up to date.
steps.pin: Need a specific release, say to match your team? kikx upgrade {flagVersion} followed by a version number installs exactly that one, older or newer.
steps.done: You know your version, how to check for a release, how to upgrade, and that your files are never part of it.
steps.why: Upgrading now and then brings new components, new templates and fixes to how files are rendered.
steps.help: kikx with the help option lists every command.
steps.helpUpgrade: upgrade is one of them, built into kikx itself: no package manager needed.
steps.confirm: Let's confirm with the version option.
steps.confirmLine: The new version is the one that runs from now on.
steps.reinstall: Running the install script again does the same job, if you prefer it.
steps.filesSame: Every vendored file is untouched too, like site.yml.
steps.pinCheck: Add the check option to see what pinning would do before you do it.
steps.pinLine: Without the check option, kikx would install that release instead.
